memory_candidates.content: When a mktemp-based bash test fixture fails with an unexpected exit code (e.g. exit 2 instead of 0/6) that the suite's own assertions don't explain, manually reproduce the fixture-builder's exact copy sequence (same REQUIRED_LIBS/REQUIRED_SCRIPTS allowlist, same mktemp root) outside the harness and run the subject script directly -- this surfaces the real stderr (e.g. a missing shared-library dependency) that the suite's captured .err files discard in their own pass/fail summary.

A fixture-based bash test suite that copies a fixed REQUIRED_LIBS/REQUIRED_SCRIPTS allowlist into an isolated mktemp repo can silently bit-rot when the subject script under test gains a new sourced library dependency via a separate, later commit -- the suite's own file list never auto-tracks the subject's actual source/dependency graph, so the drift surfaces only as an opaque exit-2 failure in unrelated test runs, not a clear 'missing dependency' message at the point the new dependency was added.
